impl:b12a1-structure.summary:
Package b12a1-structure (B12.0-B12.6) is built and committed on ccr-ccc6d89a-5cxd7e, one commit per item (B12.2 is a throwaway spike with no commit, as specified). Checkpoint S is met; checkpoint A1 is NOT met and its stop rule fired, so the package stops with the numbers and nothing was re-baselined or loosened.

Default build: the switch is off, guard printed GUARD: ALL GREEN before every commit, and the off-identity test (114 rows: SVG, route and route_partial hashes of the start commit) passes. No README, CHANGELOG or version change; the only Cargo.toml change is the check-cfg lint entry. No name, label or number of the local analog entered the repository.

Checkpoint S (met): the corridor spike routes the analog at the experiment's block positions in 1.93 and 1.98 ms against the 2.88 ms limit (unchanged route() there: 3.46 / 3.17). Its worst drag frame is over its limit (6.85 / 6.05 against 5.69), which is reported, not gated.

Checkpoint A1 (not met), with the switch on, judged from the workspace (155 checks, 19 must-fails):
- Static crossings above the must: analog 21 (must 20); permutations 21 / 32 / 21 / 21 / 40 (musts 20 / 23 / 20 / 20 / 22); public fixture and its four permutations 9 (must 7); dense-td 151 (must 74.6, start 66).
- More starts do not help: the analog is at 21 from the second start on, the public fixture at 9 from the first.
- Other A1 musts that failed: a run through a foreign frame on dense-td and notes/fork-twins (1 each); the judge's bands string on three analog permutations (the band sets and their flow order are the same, the order across the flow inside a band differs); canvas breadth of perm-e 10.3 % below the analog's; fan_x 1 / 2 / 5 on v2 / perm-b / perm-e; static hard zeros not 0 on 7 inputs and on 29 of the 200 generated block diagrams (52 before blocks).
- Suite-on cargo test: 12 lib and 8 tests/quality.rs failures. Seven are tests the spec says must pass as written (the advanced.mmd tests, note links, the composite own-state edge, the own-frame lane test, the hub-fed row wrap); I did not analyse them to the cause.
- What holds: the analog's layers and five upstream edges exactly as the spec lists them, under all five permutations; the same band sets on the public fixture's four permutations; no run through a foreign frame on the analog family, the public fixture, bench-75 and dense-lr; the two level-order constraints on every block fixture and the generated sweep; scene_ms inside its limit on the five gated inputs on two runs (dense-td 47.9 / 49.2 against 50.68); harness total static x_drawn over tests/fixtures/quality 390 against the start's 405 (bench-75 294 -> 224, dense-lr 45 -> 15); both declaration-order tests pass as written.

Where the extra crossings come from, as far as I looked: the ordering reaches 5 layered crossings on the public fixture, but the router takes edges entering a block's first row under its title chip round to the member's side (title-clear entries are b12a2's). On dense-td the middle band is one block as wide as the drawing, so every edge from the first band to the third now runs round it instead of through it.

Three things to know before the next package:
- I departed from the letter of L3 in one point: a plain node nothing links into starts neither walk. By the letter, the public fixture with its actors reversed stacked its shared services below the clusters they feed and failed "same bands".
- An earlier state of the ordering drew the analog with 18 and the public fixture with 8, but it depended on the order of the edge statements, which O4 forbids, so I did not keep it.
- Timings were taken on the shared machine at load 1.2-3.0 with no rustc running. The default build's route and drag times equal the start within that noise (each file has at least one run inside its budget). The route_partial worst frame on dense-td reads 6.00 / 5.96 ms in the test build (start 5.68 / 5.55); a third run under load read 8.47 and tripped the test's own 8 ms. I put the 0.3 ms down to the test-only block-mode recording added in B12.1, which I did not confirm.

verify:b12a1-structure#0.notes:
The verdict is fail because checkpoint A1's gate is not met, not because anything shipped is broken. The default build is safe to keep on the branch: guard is green, perf is within budget, and every output I could compare is byte-identical to the start commit. The implementer's report is accurate; I reproduced its numbers (judge output, crossings x starts table, suite-on failing tests) exactly.

Decision for the lead: the fix round should either build and measure the missing O2 exchange and analyse the seven must-pass tests, or you rule that the drawn-crossing musts cannot be judged before b12a2's title-clear entries exist. I could not confirm the implementer's explanation that the ordering reaches 5 layered crossings on the public fixture and the router adds the rest. From the picture (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-flowmaid/cac93b13-7009-5470-94b5-477c61df0333/scratchpad/verify/b12a1-structure/pic/overview-on.png), four of the nine crossings are the 'deploy' chain running across four descending edges, which looks like ordering rather than routing. On dense-td the implementer's own numbers put the layered count at 98, already above the must of 74.6, so geometry alone does not explain that one.

Other observations, none blocking on their own:
- Checkpoint S: the gated route_ms is met (2.10 / 2.37 against 2.88). The analog's worst drag frame with the spike read 8.42 / 8.67 ms on my runs against its 5.69 limit (reported, not gated; the implementer saw 6.85 / 6.05). Unchanged route() at the same positions reads 8.21 / 8.62. b12a3 has real work there.
- The generated sweep fires the lane rule on 52 of 160 random flowcharts. That may be right for random edges, but it means a third of them are not laid out as blocks; worth a look when LANE_SHARE is reviewed.
- With the switch on, frames are far broader than their content (the public fixture's shared-services and observability frames span the drawing). That is b12a2's X and F work and expected at this checkpoint.
- FLOWMAID_RECORD_IDENTITY re-records the identity table from inside the test and returns without asserting. It is test-only, but a CI job that set it would pass trivially.
